lessons.claim: ★★ **Verifying a potential by its energy alone is not verifying its force.** It actually bit -- verify_angle_matrix.py measured the bending stiffness as k = 2U/δ², got a 0.55% agreement with HOOMD and PASSed, while in the same configuration **the force was up to 96% wrong** (the sinθ clamp of angle.Harmonic). The energy was computed straight from arccos and was exact; only the force broke, on the 1/sinθ route. ★ The irony is that the **reason** for choosing the energy was right -- the per-particle force array may not be in tag order because of ParticleSorter, so the scalar energy was chosen to avoid the ordering problem. That choice hid the trap. The rule: for a new potential or force, **compare the force directly against the numerical gradient of the energy (Richardson extrapolation)**. Solve the ordering problem by inverse-permuting with the local snapshot's tags (out[tags]=F) rather than avoiding it. An auxiliary check: for an internal potential the forces must sum to 0.
